Analysis is two levels too high, which inflates the module's analysis share used for the Blueprint skill mix.
evidence: ppe-19 asks only for the treatment of interest earned (ASC 835-20-30-10). ppe-26's $55,839 is never used in any calculation; the key is 'Capitalize it with a liability'. ppe-27 is the same fact as ppe-15, which is labeled application/difficulty 1. The same ARO fact appears in ppe-08 and ppe-14, both labeled application/difficulty 2. cues.md label distribution counts 11 'analysis' items; after relabeling, only far-ppe-09 is plausibly analysis.
source: AICPA 2026 Blueprint skill definitions (Remembering and Understanding vs Analysis); FAR-II.D.1 is the recall task for capitalized costs, capitalized interest and AROs (review/reference/blueprint-tasks.csv)
fix: Relabel far-ppe-19, far-ppe-26 and far-ppe-27 to skill 'remembering', difficulty 1. Set calc:false on far-ppe-26 or drop the dollar figure. Alternatively, rewrite them as true analysis items, e.g., give a set of expenditures and ask which are misclassified.

issue: Thin or circular explanations. Item-level explanations state the rule but not the computation. Several distractor explanations say only 'Not the computation.' / 'Not the treatment.' / 'It's capitalized.' and never say what error produces the wrong number. All of these distractors are in fact traceable to a specific error.
evidence: Item-level explanations with no numbers: ppe-12, 13, 17, 21, 22, 23, 24, 25, 28, x2-21, x2-34. Correct-choice explanations with no numbers: ppe-13 d, ppe-17 a (10,000 × $25 never shown), ppe-24 d, ppe-25 a. 'Not the computation.' with the traceable error it hides: ppe-21 d $109,500 = 100,000 + 3,000 + 5,000 + 1,500 (gross price plus the repair). ppe-22 d $215,000 = 200,000 + 15,000 (salvage and title ignored). ppe-23 b $100,000 = 1,000,000 × 10% (general rate on all WAAE). ppe-25 d $20,000 = 30,000 − 10,000 (cash subtracted). ppe-28 b $250,000 = 450,000 − 150,000 − 50,000 (residual method); ppe-28 c $225,000 = 450,000 ÷ 2. Other circular explanations: 'Not the treatment.' (ppe-19 b, ppe-27 b), 'That is not the rule.' (ppe-27 d), 'It's capitalized.'/'It's recognized.' (ppe-26 a, c), 'They're expensed.' (ppe-18 d).
source: Review brief §2 per-MCQ check 4 (explanations state the rule and show the computation)
fix: Add the full computation to each item-level explanation (e.g., ppe-12: 900,000 × 300/1,000 = 270,000; ppe-17: 10,000 × $25 = 250,000, par 10,000 to common stock and 240,000 to APIC). Replace each 'Not the computation.' with the error the number models (as in the evidence) and relabel those traps from 'distractor-number' to the real misconception (partial-computation / wrong-rule).

issue: Distractor explanations or trap labels misstate the misconception or the rule. I reproduced every numeric distractor in the batch from its stem in python to find the error that actually produces it.
evidence: ppe-23 a ($80,000 = 1,000,000 × 8%) says 'Use the specific rate first', but this distractor DID use the specific rate. The error is applying 8% beyond the $600,000 loan (correct: 600,000 × 8% + 400,000 × 10% = 88,000), so the trap is overgeneralization, not wrong-rule. ppe-06 d says the first expenditure 'is when capitalization begins'. Under ASC 835-20-25-5, capitalization begins only when all three conditions are present (expenditures, activities, interest incurred), which is the key of ppe-20, so the two items contradict each other. ppe-15 c: 'Capitalized costs are depreciated, not expensed ratably' — depreciation is ratable expensing, so the explanation muddles the point (the real error is expensing over the extension period instead of depreciating the asset's new carrying amount over its remaining life). ppe-20 c ('When project debt is first issued') and ppe-09 b ('keep the old roof on the books') are labeled partial-computation, but neither involves a computation; they are wrong-rule / incomplete derecognition. far-x2-06 d ($1,005,000) says it 'Omits the legal fees', but omitting the legal fees gives 1,000,000 + 50,000 − 5,000 = 1,045,000. The 1,005,000 actually comes from 1,000,000 − 5,000 + 10,000: the demolition cost is omitted while the salvage is still deducted. Trap-label inconsistency for identical errors: omitting the cash discount is labeled partial-computation in chk1 b ($54,000) but wrong-rule in ppe-21 c ($108,000 = 100,000 + 3,000 + 5,000). Ignoring the salvage is labeled partial-computation in ppe-01 b and x2-06 b but wrong-rule in ppe-22 a ($217,000 = 200,000 + 15,000 + 2,000). Every other numeric distractor in the batch reproduces as its explanation states: chk1, ppe-01, 02, 04, 05, 07, 09, 12, 13, 17, 24, 25, x2-07, x2-21 and x2-34 (the 'Not the computation.' cases are covered by finding 003).
fix: ppe-23 a: 'Applies the 8% specific rate to all 1,000,000 of WAAE; only the 600,000 covered by the loan uses 8%' (trap overgeneralization). ppe-06 d: 'Capitalization begins only when expenditures, construction activities and interest cost are all present; the first expenditure alone does not start or end it.' ppe-15 c: explain that the capitalized cost is added to the truck and depreciated over its remaining (extended) life. Relabel ppe-20 c and ppe-09 b to wrong-rule. far-x2-06 d: 'Omits the $50,000 demolition cost but still deducts the $5,000 salvage; net demolition is a land cost' (trap partial-computation). Alternatively, change the option to $1,045,000 to keep the current explanation. Relabel ppe-21 c and ppe-22 a to partial-computation, consistent with chk1 b, ppe-01 b and x2-06 b.

issue: Answer cues. In ppe-06 the key is by far the longest option and the only one with technical qualifiers ('substantially complete and ready for its intended use'). In ppe-20 the key 'When three conditions are met' is the only option that names no event. It cannot be checked against knowledge of the rule and can be guessed by elimination.
evidence: cues.md flags ppe-06: 'key much longest; key repeats most stem words'. ppe-06 option lengths: a 74 characters vs b 42, c 57, d 34. In ppe-20 the explanation names the three conditions, but the option does not, so a candidate who knows the rule cannot confirm it from the option text, and a candidate who does not know it picks the odd-one-out.
fix: ppe-06: lengthen the distractors to parallel form (e.g., 'When the construction loan is repaid in full and the lender releases its lien', 'When the building is occupied by employees for the first time'). ppe-20: make the key 'When expenditures have been made, construction activities are in progress, and interest cost is being incurred', with parallel distractors that list two of the three conditions or substitute a wrong one (e.g., board approval).

issue: Exact duplicate across pools. Practice item ppe-23 and exam-pool item far-x2-21 use the same facts (WAAE 1,000,000; 600,000 construction loan at 8%; other debt at 10%) and the same key, 88,000. A learner who practiced ppe-23 meets the same problem on a mock, which inflates mock and readiness scores.
evidence: Both: 600,000 × 8% = 48,000 + 400,000 × 10% = 40,000 = 88,000. Distractors 48,000 and 100,000 appear in both. Only the actual-interest wording differs ('exceeds the result' vs $150,000).
fix: Re-number one of them. Ideally rewrite far-x2-21 so the actual-interest cap binds (e.g., actual interest $70,000 → capitalize 70,000) or so the general-debt weighted-average rate must be computed (see the coverage finding).

issue: Redundancy. Several single facts are tested the same way three or four times in this 32-MCQ module, and the late-numbered items add nothing.
evidence: (1) Life-extending expenditure → capitalize: chk2, ppe-15 (engine extends life), ppe-27 (roof extends life), plus ppe-09. (2) ARO → Dr asset / Cr ARO: ppe-08, ppe-14, ppe-26, plus fc6. (3) Lump-sum relative fair value allocation: ppe-02, ppe-12, ppe-28. (4) Land cost = price + demolition − salvage + title/legal: pre1, ppe-01, ppe-22, far-x2-06. ppe-22 and x2-06 have the same structure.
source: Review brief §2 per-MCQ check 7 (same fact tested the same way more than about 3 times)
fix: Repurpose the four redundant items to cover untested areas. ppe-27: roof replacement when the old roof's cost is unknown (debit accumulated depreciation). ppe-26: subsequent ARO accretion and depreciation in year 1. ppe-28: lump-sum purchase where one asset's fair value is unknown, or a classification set with mixed land/building/equipment costs. ppe-22: purchase with a noninterest-bearing note recorded at present value.

issue: The 'lesser of avoidable and actual interest' limit never binds anywhere in the module. Every capitalized-interest problem (lesson worked example, faded example, ppe-04, ppe-23, x2-07, x2-21, TBS far-tbs-u6-ppe) has actual interest far above avoidable interest. Also, the weighted-average rate on general debt is always given, never computed from several issues, and no item has a specific loan larger than WAAE. The exam's usual twists are therefore never practiced.
evidence: Avoidable vs actual: worked 75,000 vs 240,000; faded 99,000 vs 270,000; ppe-04 155,000 vs 505,000; ppe-23 88,000 vs 'exceeds'; x2-07 180,000 vs 400,000; x2-21 88,000 vs 150,000; TBS 78,000 vs 300,000. No item asks for a weighted rate such as (2,000,000 × 10% + 1,000,000 × 7%) ÷ 3,000,000 = 9%. In ppe-04 and x2-07 the stem supplies 'a weighted-average rate of 10%'.
source: ASC 835-20-30-2 to 30-6 (avoidable interest, specific and weighted-average rates, limit at interest actually incurred); review/reference/far-standards.md Part 3 (capitalized interest)
fix: Add (or convert ppe-23/x2-21 into) at least one MCQ where actual interest is below avoidable interest, and one where the general-debt rate must be computed from two or more issues. Optionally make the faded example's debt smaller so that the cap binds.

issue: Sequencing and routing. These nonmonetary-exchange items (ASC 845) are tagged moduleId far-ppe-acquisition, but exchanges are taught in the next module, far-depreciation ('Depreciation, disposals & exchanges'), whose objectives and its own items cover them. Module practice for this module (PracticeStart builds a quiz from moduleIds:[moduleId]) therefore serves exchange questions before the concept is taught. Misses route the learner to a lesson that never mentions exchanges. Also, ppe-25 opens with 'The same exchange', which refers to another item, though items are served in shuffled order.
evidence: The far-ppe-acquisition lesson has no mention of exchanges or commercial substance. far-depreciation/lesson.md line 12 objective: 'Record disposals and nonmonetary exchanges with and without commercial substance'; it has a 'Nonmonetary exchanges' section (line 104) and its own exchange items (questions.json, lines 73, 315 and 350). The keys themselves are correct: ppe-24 50,000 / 10,000 gain; ppe-25 30,000 + 10,000 = 40,000; x2-34 60,000 / 10,000 gain.
source: content/sections/far.yaml module order; far-depreciation lesson; ASC 845-10-30-1 and 30-3
fix: Change moduleId to far-depreciation for far-ppe-24, far-ppe-25 and far-x2-34. Reword the ppe-25 stem as a standalone item ('An asset with a $30,000 book value and $40,000 fair value plus $10,000 cash is exchanged for a new asset; the exchange lacks commercial substance...').

issue: Lesson–item alignment gaps. The module's items and TBS test several rules the lesson never teaches: self-constructed asset costs (incremental vs allocated overhead, abnormal costs such as rework, which is Blueprint task FAR-II.D.2); donated assets; assets acquired by issuing stock; interest earned on unspent borrowings; repairs of damage in transit or during installation; when capitalization of interest ends; and the derecognition loss on a replaced component.
evidence: ppe-13 (incremental overhead, $10,000 rework expensed) — the lesson covers only capitalized interest for self-constructed assets. ppe-10 (donation from a non-owner → contribution revenue at fair value, ASC 958-605) — not in the lesson. ppe-17 (stock issued for land) — taught only later, in far-equity. ppe-19 (interest earned not offset, ASC 835-20-30-10) — not in the lesson. chk1, ppe-21 and far-tbs-x2-ppe row x5 (repairs of transit or installation damage expensed) — the lesson table only says 'Repairs after the asset is in use', which a literal reader would not apply to damage before use; chk1 is the inline check placed directly after that table. ppe-06 (ends when substantially complete and ready for intended use, ASC 835-20-25-5) — the lesson gives only the start conditions. ppe-09 (loss = 90,000 − 70,000 = 20,000) — the lesson says only 'remove the old component's cost if known'.
fix: Add to the lesson: (1) a short 'Self-constructed assets' paragraph (direct materials and labor, incremental overhead — not a share of fixed overhead — capitalized interest; abnormal costs such as rework, strikes and damage are expensed); (2) a table row: 'Repairs of damage in transit or during installation → expense'; (3) a 'Noncash acquisitions' box: stock issued → fair value of the shares (or of the asset, if more reliable); donated asset from a non-owner → fair value, with contribution revenue (gain); (4) one line each on when capitalization ends and on not offsetting interest earned; (5) in the improvements row: 'remove the old component's cost and accumulated depreciation and recognize a loss'.

issue: The flashcard lists 'demolition of old building (net of salvage)' as a land cost without the condition that the building was acquired with the land in order to be razed. Memorized as written, it gives the wrong answer for a company razing a building it has used, which is a loss (the lesson's own trap box; ppe-18).
evidence: fc2 back: 'Land (not depreciated): price, closing costs, title, survey, clearing, demolition of old building (net of salvage).' The lesson trap: 'Demolishing a building the company already used → loss on disposal of that building.' ppe-18 key (b): expensed as a loss.
source: ASC 360-10-30-1 (costs to prepare land for its intended use); lesson trap box
fix: Change to 'demolition of an old building acquired with the land (net of salvage)', and optionally add '(razing a building the company used → loss)'.

issue: The ddb2 and syd1 explanations show rounded intermediate figures that do not reproduce the stated answers. The ddb2 explanation also uses a roundabout depreciation-year allocation instead of the standard approach (rate × beginning book value), which gives the same number in one step. A learner checking the arithmetic is confused.
evidence: Explanation: '26,667 + ... 17,778 = 44,444'. As displayed, 26,667 + 17,778 = 44,445; unrounded it is 26,666.67 + 17,777.78 = 44,444.44. The standard method gives (160,000 − 26,666.67) × 2/6 = 44,444.44. The answer 44,444 with tolerance 1 is correct, and both 44,444 and 44,445 are accepted. syd1: the explanation shows '144,000 × 6/21 = 41,143; half = 20,571', but 41,143 ÷ 2 = 20,571.5, which rounds to 20,572. The unrounded figure is 41,142.86 ÷ 2 = 20,571.43 → 20,571, so the key is right. Every other TBS explanation figure reproduces exactly: rollforward (638,000; −135,000; 4,753,000; −111,000; 1,671,000; 6,000; 3,082,000; 18,000), subledger (2,941,400; −18,500; −25,100; 2,941,400; 700; −24,400), u6-ppe (cost, sl1, ddb1, waae, avoid, cap) and x2-ppe (211,000; 40,000; 91,000; 21,000; 30,000).
fix: Rewrite the ddb2 explanation as 'Book value at start of Year 2 = 160,000 − 26,667 = 133,333; × 2/6 = **44,444**', optionally noting that the depreciation-year allocation gives the same result. syd1: show '144,000 × 6/21 × ½ = 20,571 (41,142.86 ÷ 2)'.

issue: The explanation's rule ('recorded at the fair value of the stock or the asset, whichever is more clearly evident') is the pre-ASU 2018-07 ASC 505-50 / textbook formulation. Since ASU 2018-07, share-based payments to nonemployees for goods used in operations fall under ASC 718 and are measured at the grant-date fair value of the equity instruments. Whether PP&E such as land counts as 'goods' here was not directly confirmed. The key ($250,000) is the same under either rule because the land has no reliable appraisal.
evidence: 10,000 × $25 = 250,000 under both approaches. The search confirmed that ASU 2018-07 superseded ASC 505-50 and pulled nonemployee goods-and-services awards into ASC 718, measured at the grant-date fair value of the equity instruments (Deloitte Heads Up 2018 issue 6: https://dart.deloitte.com/USDART/home/publications/archive/deloitte-publications/heads-up/2018/fasb-simplifies-accounting-for-share-based). Its application to PP&E was not stated in the sources. Stock compensation is BAR content per review/reference/far-standards.md §1c. far-equity/lesson.md also teaches 'at the more clearly determinable fair value'.
source: ASU 2018-07; ASC 718-10-15-3; ASC 845-10-15-4 (issuance of own stock excluded from ASC 845)
fix: Reword the explanation to 'record the land at the fair value of the shares issued (10,000 × $25 = $250,000); the land has no reliable appraisal', so it is right under either framework. Have an expert confirm whether FAR content should keep the 'more clearly evident' wording platform-wide.

issue: The explanation says 'only transfers from governments to businesses are excluded' from ASC 958-605's scope. That overstates it: the scope also excludes exchange transactions, transfers in which the recipient is an agent or intermediary, and tax exemptions, incentives and abatements. The key is correct.
evidence: ASC 958-605-15-6 lists several exclusions, among them (a) exchange transactions, (b) agent/trustee/intermediary transfers, (c) tax exemptions, incentives and abatements, and (d) transfers of assets from government entities to business entities (added by ASU 2018-08).
source: ASC 958-605-15-2, 15-6 (from memory; REVIEW.md decision D3 cites 958-605-15-2, 25-2, 30-2)
fix: Change to '(transfers from governments to businesses, among other items, are excluded from its scope)' or simply drop 'only'.

issue: All four PP&E simulations list far-ppe-acquisition first in moduleIds. TBS attempts are attributed to moduleIds[0] (src/db/actions.ts:113), so misses on depreciation-method, disposal-gain and impairment rows lower this module's mastery and point the learner back to the acquisition lesson. ModulePage also links every unit-u6 TBS right after this first module, before DDB/SYD, disposals and impairment are taught.
evidence: far-tbs-u6-ppe: dep part (5 rows: SL/DDB/SYD) is taught in far-depreciation. far-tbs-x2-ppe: d, cv, im and d4 rows rely on far-depreciation and far-impairment. Rollforward: gdis, adis, aend and gain rows rely on far-depreciation (disposals). Subledger: pl.gain relies on far-depreciation. Every numeric answer was recomputed and agrees with the key (e.g., WAAE 1,225,000, avoidable 78,000; cost 211,000, impairment 21,000; gend 4,753,000, net 3,082,000; gadj 2,941,400, total −24,400).
fix: Either order moduleIds by the module that supplies most of the scored cells (e.g., far-depreciation first for the rollforward and x2-ppe), or label the unit TBS list 'complete after the unit's last module'. A row-level module attribution would be the app-side fix (outside this content batch).
